title: Area of triangles, parallelograms, trapezia and circles
summary: Move pieces to see why the area of a parallelogram is base × height, why a triangle is half of that, complete a trapezium with a copy of itself, and estimate the area of a circle.
guide: This studio follows the cut-and-move method of the Iranian grade 4 to 6 books: cut a triangle off a parallelogram and slide it across to make a rectangle; two equal triangles make a parallelogram; two equal trapezia make a parallelogram; and the area of a circle is estimated by counting squares. In England, parallelograms and triangles are Year 6; trapezia and circles come later (Key Stage 3).
Drag a piece to move it; the ↺ and ↻ buttons give it a quarter turn. With a keyboard, move to a piece and use the arrow keys. Each piece must fit exactly into the dashed gap.

The height is always at right angles to the base. Common mistakes are to multiply by the slanted side instead of the height, and to forget to halve for a triangle. Moving the pieces shows that the area does not change.

engine.letters: A B C D E F G H I J
engine.instruction-move: Drag the piece into the dashed gap.

slide-triangle.title: Turn a parallelogram into a rectangle
slide-triangle.prompt: A triangle has been cut off this {{term:parallelogram}}. Drag the triangle into the dashed gap. What shape do you make?
slide-triangle.hint: Slide the triangle to the right until its slanted side sits against the slanted side at the other end.
slide-triangle.success: Well done! The parallelogram has become a 4 by 3 {{term:rectangle}}.
slide-triangle.why: Did the area change when you moved the triangle? What is the area of the parallelogram?
slide-triangle.model: No. Nothing was added or taken away; one piece just moved. The rectangle is 4 × 3 = 12, so the parallelogram is 12 too. The rectangle's length is the parallelogram's base and its width is the parallelogram's height: area of a parallelogram = base × height.

feedback.not-fit: The triangle does not fit the dashed gap yet. Slide it to the right until the gap is completely filled.

parallelogram-area.title: Base × height
parallelogram-area.prompt: This parallelogram has a base of 6 and a slanted side of 5. The red dashed line is its height. What is its area in square units?
parallelogram-area.hint: Count the squares to find the height. Remember: area of a parallelogram = base × height, not base × slanted side.
parallelogram-area.why: Why don't we multiply the base by the slanted side (5)?
parallelogram-area.model: If we cut off the triangle at the side and move it across, we get a rectangle 4 tall, not 5. The slanted side leans over, so it does not show how tall the shape is; the height, at right angles to the base, does.

feedback.slant: 6 × 5 = 30. You used the slanted side. The height is the dashed line at right angles to the base: count its squares.
feedback.perimeter: 22 is the perimeter: 6 + 5 + 6 + 5. We want the area.
feedback.halved: Halving is only for a triangle. Moving one piece turns a parallelogram into a whole rectangle.
feedback.too-big: That is more than the area. Multiply the base by the height.
feedback.too-small: That is less than the area. Multiply the base by the height.

two-triangles.title: Two equal triangles
two-triangles.prompt: Here are two equal {{term:triangle}}s. Turn the top one and drag it into the dashed gap. What shape do the two triangles make?
two-triangles.hint: The triangle needs a half turn: press a turn button twice, then drag it down.
two-triangles.success: Well done! Two equal triangles make a {{term:parallelogram}}.
two-triangles.why: The triangle has a base of 4 and a height of 3. What is the area of one triangle? Why?
two-triangles.model: Together the two triangles make a parallelogram with base 4 and height 3, so its area is 4 × 3 = 12. One triangle is half of that: 4 × 3 ÷ 2 = 6. So area of a triangle = base × height ÷ 2.

feedback.not-fit: The triangle does not fit the dashed gap yet. If it is not upside down, turn it twice; then move it until it sits exactly on the dashed outline.

house.title: The area of a house
house.prompt: This house is a rectangle (the wall) and a triangle (the roof). The dashed line is the height of the roof. What is the area of the whole house in square units?
house.hint: Find the area of the wall first, then the roof. Area of a triangle = base × height ÷ 2. Then add the two areas.
house.success: Well done! Wall 6 × 3 = 18, roof 6 × 3 ÷ 2 = 9, whole house 18 + 9 = 27 square units.
house.why: Why did you halve the area of the roof but not the area of the wall?
house.model: The roof is a triangle, and a triangle is half of a parallelogram (or rectangle) with the same base and height. If we draw a 6 by 3 rectangle round the roof, the roof fills exactly half of it. The wall is already a rectangle, so there is nothing to halve.

feedback.not-halved: 18 + 18 = 36. You did not halve the roof. The roof is a triangle: base × height ÷ 2.
feedback.walls-only: 18 is just the wall. Add the roof too.
feedback.roof-only: 9 is just the roof. Add the wall too.
feedback.too-big: That is more than the area of the house. Work out each part on its own and add them.
feedback.too-small: That is less than the area of the house. Work out each part on its own and add them.

two-trapezia.title: Two equal trapezia
two-trapezia.prompt: This {{term:trapezium}} has parallel sides of 5 and 2 and a height of 2. Turn the top trapezium and drag it into the dashed gap. What shape do the two trapezia make?
two-trapezia.hint: It needs a half turn: press a turn button twice. Then drag it until its slanted side sits against the slanted side of the bottom trapezium.
two-trapezia.success: Well done! The two trapezia make a {{term:parallelogram}}.
two-trapezia.why: What is the area of one trapezium? Use the parallelogram you made.
two-trapezia.model: The parallelogram's base is 5 + 2 = 7 and its height is 2, so its area is 7 × 2 = 14. Each trapezium is half of it: 14 ÷ 2 = 7. So area of a trapezium = (sum of the parallel sides) × height ÷ 2.

feedback.not-fit: The trapezium does not fit the dashed gap yet. If it is not upside down, turn it twice; then move it.

circle-estimate.title: Estimate the area of a circle
circle-estimate.prompt: This {{term:circle}} has a radius of 3. The big square round it has 36 squares and the dashed diamond inside has 18. Which number is closest to the area of the circle?
circle-estimate.hint: The circle is bigger than the diamond and smaller than the square. Count the whole squares inside it and count part squares two for one.
circle-estimate.success: Well done! The area is about 28 square units: radius × radius × π = 3 × 3 × 3.14 = 28.26
circle-estimate.why: Why is 9 (radius × radius) not the answer?
circle-estimate.model: 3 × 3 = 9 is the area of a small 3 by 3 square, only a quarter of the big square. The circle is bigger than the 18-square diamond. For the area of a circle we multiply radius × radius by π (about 3.14).

feedback.wrong: Look again: the circle is bigger than the dashed diamond (18), but it does not fill the whole square (36). And 9 is only radius × radius.
